## Intent [Codiff](https://github.com/nkzw-tech/codiff) is a local desktop diff viewer for reviewing GitHub pull requests: it shows side-by-side diffs, can run an AI walkthrough, posts comments to GitHub, and can jump into an editor. It only works inside a local clone of the repository, though, and has no way to clone one or clean it up afterwards. Reviewing many pull requests therefore means cloning, checking out and deleting by hand again and again. This adds `codiff-helper`, a small command-line companion that removes that repetition: - `codiff-helper ` makes a fast partial clone into its own folder, `~/Reviews///pr-` (the root can be changed with `CODIFF_HELPER_ROOT`), switches it to the pull request's latest commits, and opens Codiff there with the AI walkthrough started. `--no-walkthrough` skips the walkthrough and `--agent ` is passed through to Codiff. - Running it again updates the copy to the latest commits and opens it; a copy with local edits is left untouched, with a warning. - Merged or closed pull requests still open, with a one-line note. - `codiff-helper --done` deletes the copy. It only ever deletes folders it created, and refuses while anything local is not on GitHub (changed, untracked or unpushed work) unless `--force` is given. Plain `codiff-helper --done` inside a review folder works on that folder. `codiff-helper --list` shows the copies on disk. There is no delete-everything option. - GitHub only, including private repositories and pull requests from forks, through the existing `gh` login. The editor is reached through Codiff's own open-in-editor action rather than opened directly. - Written in .NET 10 / C# and installed by `install.sh`, which builds one fast-starting native program into `~/.local/bin`. - The README states that this is an unofficial companion to Codiff, not made by Codiff's authors. ## What Changed - Adds the codiff-helper .NET 10 CLI (`src/CodiffHelper`): given a pull request URL, it creates or updates a review copy at `~/Reviews///pr-` via a fast partial clone, switches it to the pull request's latest commits, and opens Codiff with the AI walkthrough started (`--no-walkthrough` and `--agent ` supported; merged/closed pull requests open with a one-line note, and copies with local edits are left untouched with a warning). - Adds cleanup and inspection commands: `--done` deletes a review copy, refusing while any work is not on GitHub unless `--force` is passed (plain `codiff-helper --done` works inside a review folder), and `--list` shows the review copies on disk. - Adds `install.sh` (single native binary into `~/.local/bin`, overridable via `CODIFF_HELPER_INSTALL_DIR`), solution/build setup (`.gitignore`, `global.json`, `codiff-helper.slnx`), README documentation, and a full test suite covering URL parsing, review storage, and the open/done/list flows. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: the implementation is careful about what it deletes (only folders it created, only inside the reviews root, no following symlinks, refusing while local work exists), and the external command contracts were checked against the installed gh and Codiff. Review raised three components that went beyond the design; all three are settled: the `--agent=` inline form and the unused head-commit lookup were removed, and the `--list` title, state and local-changes columns (with the saved offline fallback) were kept because the design asked for them. ## Testing Drove the compiled codiff-helper binary end-to-end with the owner's real signed-in gh, real git, and real GitHub using public octocat/Hello-World pull requests (including fork PRs and a merged PR whose head branch is gone), with only the codiff GUI launcher fronted by a recording stub so the owner's desktop app is never opened; every intent behavior — clone layout, PR-head checkout, walkthrough/agent passthrough, local-edit protection, merged-PR note, --list, all --done guard rails, root settings, and install.sh — behaved as specified, and the two owner-approved review fixes (--agent= removal, headRefOid removal) were confirmed live. The README disclaimer and the real-GUI launch were not driven live and are recorded as untested. - Live validation: ✅ go - 12 of 14 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Open a pull request URL: partial-clones into <root>/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<number>, checks out the PR's latest commit, and launches codiff with the AI walkthrough from that folder | ✅ pass | live | live-session-transcript.txt: local HEAD b308ed63... equals gh's headRefOid; stub recorded 'codiff -w <url>' with cwd = review folder | | Re-running the same URL when nothing changed reports up-to-date and reopens | ✅ pass | live | Earlier live run: 'octocat/Hello-World#11301 is already up to date' + second codiff invocation | | Local edits are protected: re-run warns and leaves the copy untouched instead of updating it | ✅ pass | live | live-session-transcript.txt: warning line + 'README tail: my note' preserved | | A merged pull request still opens, with a one-line note saying so (including the deleted-fork-head fallback to refs/pull/<n>/head) | ✅ pass | live | live-session-transcript.txt: 'note: octocat/Hello-World#6 is merged'; HEAD matched gh head 76294131... | | --no-walkthrough skips the walkthrough and --agent <name> is passed through to codiff; the undocumented --agent= form is rejected | ✅ pass | live | Stub recorded args [--agent, pi, <url>] with no -w; '--agent=pi' produced 'unknown option' with exit 2 | | --list shows the review copies on disk with their state and local-work flag, ignores folders it did not create, and reports an empty root | ✅ pass | live | Live --list output with 3 rows (one flagged 'local changes'), non-helper pr-999 excluded, 'No review copies' after cleanup | | --done refuses when anything local is not on GitHub (changed file, untracked file, unpushed commit), naming each, and keeps the folder | ✅ pass | live | live-session-transcript.txt refusal block; Intent

Codiff is a local desktop diff viewer for reviewing GitHub pull requests: it shows side-by-side diffs, can run an AI walkthrough, posts comments to GitHub, and can jump into an editor. It only works inside a local clone of the repository, though, and has no way to clone one or clean it up afterwards. Reviewing many pull requests therefore means cloning, checking out and deleting by hand again and again.

This adds codiff-helper, a small command-line companion that removes that repetition:

  • codiff-helper <pull request URL> makes a fast partial clone into its own folder, ~/Reviews/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<number> (the root can be changed with CODIFF_HELPER_ROOT), switches it to the pull request's latest commits, and opens Codiff there with the AI walkthrough started. --no-walkthrough skips the walkthrough and --agent <name> is passed through to Codiff.
  • Running it again updates the copy to the latest commits and opens it; a copy with local edits is left untouched, with a warning.
  • Merged or closed pull requests still open, with a one-line note.
  • codiff-helper <url> --done deletes the copy. It only ever deletes folders it created, and refuses while anything local is not on GitHub (changed, untracked or unpushed work) unless --force is given. Plain codiff-helper --done inside a review folder works on that folder. codiff-helper --list shows the copies on disk. There is no delete-everything option.
  • GitHub only, including private repositories and pull requests from forks, through the existing gh login. The editor is reached through Codiff's own open-in-editor action rather than opened directly.
  • Written in .NET 10 / C# and installed by install.sh, which builds one fast-starting native program into ~/.local/bin.
  • The README states that this is an unofficial companion to Codiff, not made by Codiff's authors.

What Changed

  • Adds the codiff-helper .NET 10 CLI (src/CodiffHelper): given a pull request URL, it creates or updates a review copy at ~/Reviews/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<number> via a fast partial clone, switches it to the pull request's latest commits, and opens Codiff with the AI walkthrough started (--no-walkthrough and --agent <name> supported; merged/closed pull requests open with a one-line note, and copies with local edits are left untouched with a warning).
  • Adds cleanup and inspection commands: --done deletes a review copy, refusing while any work is not on GitHub unless --force is passed (plain codiff-helper --done works inside a review folder), and --list shows the review copies on disk.

Risk Assessment
